plan: This is a second-price auction where bidding my true value is the dominant strategy. Since I pay the second-highest bid (not my own bid) if I win, bidding exactly my value of $31 maximizes my expected profit - I win whenever my value exceeds others' bids and pay less than my value, and I don't want to risk winning at a price above my value or losing a profitable opportunity. No history exists to suggest deviation from this optimal strategy.

This is a second-price auction where bidding my true value is the dominant strategy. Since I pay the second-highest bid (not my own bid) if I win, bidding exactly my value of $46 maximizes my expected profit - if I win, I pay less than my value (profit), and if I lose, someone else valued it more than me. There's no incentive to shade my bid up or down from my true valuation.

This is a second-price auction format where the winner pays the second-highest bid, not their own bid. In this mechanism, bidding my true value is the dominant strategy - it maximizes my expected profit regardless of what others bid. If I bid higher than my value, I risk winning at a price above my value (negative profit). If I bid lower, I risk losing auctions I could have profitably won. Therefore, I should bid exactly $35, my true value.
